mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% signals deteriorating industrial production, reflecting weakening manufacturing activity and reduced corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over the same month indicates a shift from inventory accumulation to demand weakness, which signals impending softening of economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy with declining inflation, which typically supports stable growth and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND CPIAUCSL < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.4% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.4% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS for three consecutive months signals weakening household savings and consumption intent, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < 0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.
